message.content:
**C♯ Major Scale**

The C♯ major scale consists of the following seven notes (plus the octave):

| Degree | Note |
|--------|------|
| 1 (Tonic) | C♯ |
| 2 | D♯ |
| 3 | E♯ (enharmonic to F) |
| 4 | F♯ |
| 5 | G♯ |
| 6 | A♯ |
| 7 | B♯ (enharmonic to C) |
| 8 (Octave) | C♯ |

**Key Signature:**  
C♯ major has **seven sharps**: F♯, C♯, G♯, D♯, A♯, E♯, and B♯.

**Notes on Enharmonics:**  
- E♯ is the same pitch as F natural.  
- B♯ is the same pitch as C natural.  

So, the C♯ major scale can also be written as:  
C♯ – D♯ – F – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – C – C♯ (if you prefer to use the enharmonic equivalents).
